text: You receive an assignment that is due in one week. What usually happens first?
labels: I decide early when I will work on it.
I keep it in mind but do not make a concrete plan.
I usually start when the deadline gets closer.
I sometimes lose track of assignments like this.

text: You have several assignments due in the same week. How do you usually handle them?
labels: I prioritize them and plan my time.
I work through them one by one without much of a plan.
I switch between tasks depending on what feels most urgent.
I often do not know where to start.

text: You know you need to work on an important task, but it feels quite large. What usually happens?
labels: I start with one small first step.
I think about it for a while and start later.
I postpone it until there is more time pressure.
I often do not know how to begin.

text: You still have several days before an assignment is due. How likely are you to start working on it already?
labels: I usually start closer to the deadline.

text: You do not understand something important during class. What do you usually do?
labels: I try to solve it on my own first.
I usually leave it unresolved for now.

text: You are working on an assignment and have been stuck for a while. What usually happens?
labels: I ask for help relatively quickly.
I keep trying on my own for a while.
I switch to something else first.
I often stay stuck for a long time without asking anyone.

text: You have studied a topic. How do you usually check whether you really understood it?
labels: I test myself or try to explain it to someone.
I work on exercises related to it.
I read through my notes again.
I usually do not really check.

text: You receive a solution to an assignment, but you do not understand why it works. What do you usually do?
labels: I try to understand why the solution works.
I ask someone to explain it.
I mainly remember the steps used in the solution.
I move on as long as I managed to complete the task.

text: Several deadlines fall into the same week. How do you usually react?
labels: I organize the tasks and work through them by priority.
I feel some pressure but usually keep track of everything.
I partially lose track of what needs to be done.
I quickly feel blocked and do not know where to start.

text: You receive a difficult assignment that you have never done before. What is your typical first reaction?
labels: I assume I can work it out step by step.
I feel unsure but start anyway.
I wait because I am worried about doing it wrong.
I quickly think that I probably cannot do it.

text: How well did you keep track of your assignments and deadlines this week?
labels: I kept track of most things.
I lost track of some things.
I lost track of several things.

text: How often did you start an assignment later than you originally intended this week?
When you did not understand something or got stuck this week, how quickly did you ask for help?
labels: I did not ask even though I needed help.
I did not need help this week.

text: How often did you forget that an assignment or deadline was coming up this week?
How often did you clearly know what you should work on next this week?
How often did you postpone an assignment this week even though you actually had time to work on it?
When a task felt large or unclear this week, how well were you able to identify a first step?
Was there a situation this week where you probably should have asked for help but did not?
How easy was it for you this week to tell a teacher, mentor, or classmate that you did not understand something?
How often did you have the feeling this week: "I completed it, but I did not really understand it"?
How often did you actively check whether you really understood a topic this week?
labels: I did not know how to check.

text: How often did you feel this week that too many things were happening at the same time?
How well were you able to decide what was most important when you had several tasks this week?
When you encountered a difficult assignment this week, what did you usually think?
labels: This will be difficult, but I will try.
I quickly thought that I probably could not do it.

text: How often did you start an assignment this week even though you were not sure you could solve it correctly?
labels: There was no situation like this.
